note: WAEC Civic round 8 (R45 top-up): constitutional democracy; independence of the judiciary; presumption of innocence; probity; religious intolerance; volunteerism; self-esteem; goal setting; time management; consumer rights; minimum wage; strike; gender discrimination; social security; national flower (Costus spectabilis); tiers of government; environmental sanitation; peacekeeping; declaration of assets; due process; bail; National Human Rights Commission; right to property; election violence; tree planting. Scanned against the whole Civic pool (WAEC and NECO stems).

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.topic: Democracy and the Rule of Law
questions.q: A system of government in which the people's elected representatives rule, but only within the limits that the constitution sets, is called
questions.explanation: The constitution holds the leash of power.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.topic: Constitution, Rule of Law and Arms of Government
questions.q: The arrangement by which judges decide cases free from threats, sackings and interference from the president, governors or rich men is called
questions.explanation: No big man may lean on the judge's scale.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The legal principle that every person accused of a crime is treated as innocent until a court of law has proved him guilty is the
questions.explanation: The burden of proof rests on the accuser.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The strict honesty and sound character expected of a public officer, shown in complete and upright handling of public money, is called
questions.explanation: Clean hands and open books at all times.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: A citizen who hates his neighbour simply because the neighbour prays in a different way from him is displaying
questions.explanation: Another man's faith has become his offence.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: A graduate spends her Saturdays teaching pupils in an orphanage without asking for any payment. This spirit of offering service freely is
questions.explanation: Her only wage is the good she does.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: A student who knows her own worth, walks tall and speaks up in class without fear or arrogance is said to have
questions.explanation: She values herself without looking down on others.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Before the school year begins, Ada writes down that she will finish her syllabus by March and score above 80 in Civic Education. This practice is
questions.explanation: The target is chosen before the race starts.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: A trader plans her day the night before, fixing hours for market, rest and family so that no duty is swallowed by another. Her habit is
questions.explanation: Every hour is given its own work.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: When a buyer is cheated with a false measure or a spoilt tin of milk, the civic right of his that has been breached is his right as a
questions.explanation: Fair measure and true quality are his due.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The least amount an employer may legally pay a worker for a month's labour, fixed by government and reviewed from time to time, is the
questions.explanation: No lawful pay may fall beneath that floor.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The right of workers, acting together through their union, to refuse to work until their grievances are addressed is the right to
questions.explanation: The tools lie down until the talk is done.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: A firm rejects the best-qualified candidate for its manager post simply because she is a woman. This act is
questions.explanation: Her sex, not her skill, decided the matter.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The support, in money and services, which a government gives to the aged, the jobless and the disabled who cannot fully provide for themselves, is
questions.explanation: The state carries those who cannot carry themselves.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Nigeria's national flower, shown on the coat of arms, whose flat red flowers bloom close to the ground across the savanna, is the
questions.explanation: It lies on the shield's base in the arms.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The division of government in Nigeria into the federal level, the thirty-six states and the 774 local government areas is the division into
questions.explanation: Each level serves its own layer of the people.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Residents of a street come out together one Saturday to cut the grass, clear the gutters and sweep the drainage. This civic duty is
questions.explanation: A clean street is dug by every hand on it.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Nigerian soldiers serve in troubled lands under the United Nations and ECOWAS, keeping warring parties apart and protecting civilians. This service abroad is called
questions.explanation: They stand between fighters and the weak.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: On taking office, a governor publicly lists his houses, bank accounts and other wealth, and does so again when he leaves. This practice is the
questions.explanation: His pocket is opened for all to inspect.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.topic: Constitution, Rule of Law and Arms of Government
questions.q: The requirement that government business follow the correct laid-down steps — advertisement, shortlisting, interview, approval — before a contract is awarded, is
questions.explanation: No corner may be cut on the way.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: A sum of money or a surety which an accused person lodges, or a person stands for him, so that he is released from custody until his trial comes up, is
questions.explanation: He answers his charge from outside the cell.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The government body established to receive complaints from citizens whose human rights have been violated and to investigate such complaints is the
questions.explanation: The complainant's cry reaches its desk.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: The guarantee that a citizen may own land, houses and businesses, and that they cannot be seized from him without the law and fair compensation, is the
questions.explanation: What he honestly owns, he honestly keeps.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: On election day, thugs beat up voters, snatch ballot boxes and burn election materials at a polling unit. These acts are collectively
questions.explanation: The ballot is stolen by fist and fire.

questions.subject: Civic Education
questions.q: Members of a town union return every December to plant shade trees along the new road and teach pupils to water them. This service protects
questions.explanation: Every seedling is a gift to the air.
